0:00 [MUSIC] Winston Churchill is reputed to have said that
he established Jordan one afternoon in Cairo. That is an
extreme example of the arbitrary nature in which the
Middle Eastern states have been created by the great
powers of the time, Britain and France in the aftermath
of the First World War. States were created by ruler
drawn borders, by colonial officials rather than by any
other natural definition of these territorial units.
0:44 These states were established along the lines of
European nation states that are generally far more
homogeneous. At least the ideal type of the European
state, like France where people speaking French inhabit
a state called France. Or the Germans who speak
German and inhabit a state called Germany.
1:04 The Middle Eastern states were much more artificial
creations. I am Professor Asher Susser of Tel Aviv
University. And I'm going to teach a course on the
emergence of the Middle East that will explain how
these arbitrary state creations of colonial origin have
contributed to the huge destabilization and disorder
